title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: RITA'S MINIVAN
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Rita Haskins, a hospital laundry boss in Bowling Green, Kentucky.
For twenty years, she watched the county fair demolition derby from the bleachers, yelling.
This summer, she wanted a car of her own.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: BIG MARGE
segments.quote: He who has begun has half done. Dare to be wise; begin!
segments.author: Horace
lines: In March, Rita bought a rusty minivan for three hundred dollars and named it Big Marge.
Then she just stared at it for two weeks.
Her neighbor Dewey, a retired welder, handed her a wrench and a line from the Roman poet Horace:
He who has begun has half done. Dare to be wise; begin!
That night, she pulled out every seat. Half done.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE PLAN
segments.quote: Adapt or perish, now as ever, is Nature's inexorable imperative.
segments.author: H. G. Wells
lines: Rita had a plan. Drive backward, protect the engine.
In the first heat, a pickup slammed her before she found reverse.
She remembered Dewey quoting the writer H. G. Wells:
Adapt or perish, now as ever, is Nature's inexorable imperative.
Change or lose. So she drove forward and found a gap.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: STALLED
segments.quote: Fire tests gold, suffering tests brave men.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: Then Big Marge stalled, steam pouring out of the hood.
Rita wanted to wave the white flag.
But taped to her dashboard was a line from Seneca, the Roman thinker:
Fire tests gold, suffering tests brave men.
Brave women too, she figured. On the seventh turn of the key, Marge roared.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BROKEN PLACES
segments.quote: The world breaks every one and afterward many are strong at the broken places.
segments.author: Ernest Hemingway
lines: She made the final, but the frame was bent like a paper clip.
At midnight in Dewey's garage, she wanted to quit. Dewey kept welding, and quoted Ernest Hemingway:
The world breaks every one and afterward many are strong at the broken places.
By sunrise, Marge was uglier than ever, and twice as tough.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BUMPER
segments.quote: You grow up the day you have the first real laugh at yourself.
segments.author: Ethel Barrymore
lines: Before the final, the drivers rolled past the grandstand.
Marge's front bumper fell off. Clang. Three thousand people laughed.
Rita's face burned. Then she thought of the actress Ethel Barrymore:
You grow up the day you have the first real laugh at yourself.
So she held the bumper over her head and took a bow.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FINAL
segments.author: Billie Jean King
lines: Eight cars in the final. Her gloves were shaking.
Dewey leaned in and said what tennis champion Billie Jean King once told a nervous player:
Pressure is a privilege.
So Rita smiled, hit the gas, and fought to the last minute.
Second place. A forty dollar trophy. And the bleachers on their feet.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Begin. Adapt. Keep going. Grow strong. Laugh at yourself. Enjoy the pressure.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Begin. Change the plan. Keep turning the key. Get strong where you broke. Laugh at yourself. Enjoy the pressure.
I entered a go-kart race once. I came in fourth. Out of four.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
